preconditions.description: The number of houses N is an integer strictly greater than 1 and at most 100,000.
The input contains exactly N-1 lines, each describing a road as two distinct integers a and b (1 ≤ a, b ≤ N).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(a) <= N and 1 <= int(b) <= N and int(a) != int(b) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:N] for a, b in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct houses within the valid range [1, N].

preconditions.expression: len(set().union(*[set(line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:N]])) == N
preconditions.description: The roads form a connected undirected graph with exactly N-1 edges (a tree).

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is a non-negative integer representing the smallest possible total length of shortest paths.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.splitlines()[1].split()) == N and all(1 <= int(v) <= N for v in stdout.splitlines()[1].split())
postconditions.description: The second line of stdout contains exactly N space-separated integers, each representing a valid house number in [1, N].

postconditions.expression: all(int(v) != i for i, v in enumerate(stdout.splitlines()[1].split(), 1))
postconditions.description: No villager is assigned to their original house (derangement condition).

postconditions.expression: all(int(v) != int(u) for i, v in enumerate(stdout.splitlines()[1].split(), 1) for j, u in enumerate(stdout.splitlines()[1].split(), 1) if i != j)
postconditions.description: Each house in the output assignment is assigned to exactly one villager (permutation).

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.splitlines()[0]) == sum(min_distance(i, int(v)) for i, v in enumerate(stdout.splitlines()[1].split(), 1))
postconditions.description: The total length is the sum of shortest path distances from each house i to its assigned house v in the output permutation, where min_distance(i, j) is the shortest path length between houses i and j in the tree.

postconditions.expression: not any(int(stdout.splitlines()[0]) > sum(min_distance(i, int(v)) for i, v in enumerate(assignment.split(), 1)) for assignment in possible_derangements(N))
postconditions.description: The total length is the smallest possible among all valid derangements of the houses (minimality condition).
